text:
Muscle lactate production rises when glycolysis produces pyruvate faster than the mitochondria can oxidize it, as during high-intensity or sustained-maximal exercise, under hypoxia, with a high cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, or with epinephrine stimulation. The shared note is wrong: lactate is made from pyruvate by lactate dehydrogenase, which regenerates the NAD⁺ glycolysis needs, so blocking pyruvate formation would reduce lactate, not increase it.

CONFIDENCE: 90
